n2.topic: What happens if you counter the first offer by asking for a bit more
n2.why_it_hooks: Fear of the offer being pulled is the main reason people don't negotiate. The video walks through the best case, the worst case (rare, and what it signals about the employer), and the most likely case (a small move or a non-salary perk), with a polite 4-sentence counter script.

n2.topic: Rewrite It Live: the 'just circling back' follow-up that gets ignored
n2.why_it_hooks: Viewers will recognise their own follow-up emails in the weak version. Each line is rewritten to make the reply easy: a specific ask, a deadline, and a one-word answer option.

n2.topic: Rewrite It Live: 'Responsible for managing social media accounts' into a bullet a recruiter remembers
n2.why_it_hooks: A duty-style bullet is the most common resume problem. Watching it become an action, a scope and a result in three passes shows the pattern viewers can copy for their own bullets.

n2.topic: 'Quantify every bullet' is risky advice: what to do when you have no numbers
n2.why_it_hooks: It challenges a resume rule everyone repeats. The verdict is tweak: don't invent metrics. Instead, use scale, frequency, scope, before/after comparisons and stakeholder names, with example bullets for roles that have no obvious KPIs.

n2.topic: 'I'm a perfectionist' is a bad weakness answer, so here are three real ones that work
n2.why_it_hooks: The cliché answer gets rewritten line by line into an honest weakness, the specific fix you've already started, and the proof it's working. It includes a version for people who freeze and can't think of any weakness.

n2.topic: What happens if you decline a recurring meeting you don't need
n2.why_it_hooks: Everyone resents their calendar but few people dare to act. The video covers the best case (you get time back), the worst case (a manager sees it as disengagement) and the most likely case (nobody notices if you send notes). It includes a decline script that offers an async alternative.

n2.topic: What happens if you ask your manager for a four-day week at your current job
n2.why_it_hooks: It is a bold, high-curiosity move that most people have only fantasised about. The video explains why a trial proposal framed around output beats a flat request, and gives the exact pitch, the likely objections and what to say to each.

n2.topic: 'Just say no' is bad workload advice: the 'yes, and which one moves?' script
n2.why_it_hooks: The verdict is bin or tweak. A flat no rarely works with a manager, so the replacement turns the pushback into a priority decision the manager has to make. It comes with a Slack version and a spoken version.

n2.topic: Rewrite It Live: the status update that buries the blocker in paragraph four
n2.why_it_hooks: Anyone who writes updates will see their own habit. The rewrite moves the status, the risk and the ask to the top, and the video explains why managers skim and how this protects you when things slip.

n2.topic: Staying 'green' on Slack to look available is a trap: do an end-of-day note instead
n2.why_it_hooks: It goes after the remote-work habit most people feel guilty about and offers a way out. The replacement is a 3-line daily or weekly visibility message, with templates for a manager and for a wider team.

n2.topic: What happens if you correct someone in the meeting when they present your idea as theirs
n2.why_it_hooks: A clear point of tension that most people have lived through. It lays out the best case, the worst case and the likely case, then gives three levels of script: in the moment, right after the meeting, and in a written follow-up that puts your name on the idea.

n2.topic: 'Never disagree with your boss in public' is too blunt: how to disagree in a meeting without a fight
n2.why_it_hooks: It reframes a rule many people take literally. The verdict is tweak, with three scripts: asking a question that exposes the issue, adding a risk, and offering an alternative. It also covers when private really is better.

n2.topic: What happens if you reply to a rejection email and ask for feedback
n2.why_it_hooks: It's a free move almost nobody makes. The video is honest that most replies are generic or absent, shows how to phrase the ask so it's easy to answer, and covers the odd case where it reopens the door.

n2.topic: 'References available upon request' is wasting a line of your resume: what to use that space for
n2.why_it_hooks: A short, specific, easily checked tip that viewers can act on in one minute. The verdict is bin, with a list of what to use the space for instead, including a skills line, a link, and targeted keywords drawn from the job posting.

n2.topic: Rewrite It Live: a Slack message that just says 'Hey, got a minute?'
n2.why_it_hooks: It is relatable and a little funny. The video rewrites it into a message that states the topic, the urgency and the time needed, so the other person can reply asynchronously. It also shows when a quick call is still the better option.

n2.topic: What happens if you ask for a promotion outside the review cycle
n2.why_it_hooks: People assume they have to wait until review season. The video covers the best case, worst case and most likely case, explains why asking for a 'path conversation' gets more traction than asking for a title, and gives the opening script and a one-page evidence list.

n2.topic: When the interviewer says 'Any questions for us?', here are five questions that signal you're a serious candidate, and one to avoid
n2.why_it_hooks: Everyone gets this moment and most people waste it. The video gives a verdict on the popular 'ask about culture' advice, then offers sharper questions with the reasoning behind each, such as what success looks like at 90 days and what the last person in the role did well.

n2.topic: Rewrite It Live: the 'sorry for the delay' email that makes you sound junior
n2.why_it_hooks: A habit nearly every viewer has, and the fix is small and concrete. The video swaps apology for 'thanks for your patience', and shows where a genuine apology is still right. It runs through a line-by-line rewrite of a late reply.

n2.topic: What happens if you turn off work notifications after hours without telling anyone
n2.why_it_hooks: It speaks to burnout and the fear of looking disengaged. It looks at the realistic outcomes, then gives a script for setting expectations on response times and for handling a real emergency, so you protect your evenings without looking absent.
